title: It Reached the Governor
sentences: The Salem panic ended soon after it reached the governor’s own household.
Governor William Phips had set up the special court in May 1692.
By late September, it had sent nineteen people to the gallows.
Then leading ministers, including Increase Mather, spoke out against spectral evidence.
That fall, accusers reportedly named his wife, Lady Mary Phips.
On October 29th, Phips dissolved the court; many historians think the accusation played a part.
The court that replaced it condemned just three people, and none were executed.
